geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant mass from a punctured bar into a courtyard-carved body so the void becomes programmatically public.
Keep the courtyard bounded but sufficiently open for neighborhood public use.
Open the court toward the access side to align the form with the verified frontage.
Preserve a single connected mass across the split.
Add a grounded threshold datum to support the entry edge.
Expand the seam into a legible public void while keeping the wings related.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the perforation logic with a true courtyard carve so the open space becomes an occupiable public void rather than a narrow puncture.
Size the courtyard to register as a usable neighborhood void while keeping the mass compact.
Align the opening to the verified access side to strengthen the public threshold relation.
Keep the wings connected so the building remains one dominant mass rather than reading as two colliding pieces.
Strengthen the ground response along the access edge to make the entry seam more legible.
Widen the interstice enough to read as a meaningful public cut, not a technical split.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact bar with a recognizable split and some ground-level porosity, so it is not incoherent or purely box-like. The dominant gesture is legible in all views and the parcel containment appears respected. However, the public threshold is only moderately resolved: the blue access edge is answered indirectly rather than by a strong court/notch/entry seam, and the central void is too narrow to register as clearly usable public space. The silhouette is continuous but mostly planar, with only modest section variation; this weakens section-program fit for a neighborhood living brief that wants an active ground and one clear public void or terrace. Overall it is visually plausible for the program but not yet fully convincing enough for hard pass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion-like and sculptural than the candidate; its curved roof language is not directly present here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing with a central void and a bridge-like connection can create an active public threshold without fragmenting the main volume.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Scale and multiplicity are larger than the candidate; do not copy the multi-building condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A courtyard-centered campus composition can organize multiple wings while preserving a readable public core.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Its transparency and roof looseness are stronger than the candidate’s more solid, compact mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated low-rise bar with a carved central void and sloping roof can support neighborhood mixed-use well.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more spread out and sectionally expressive; the candidate is tighter and less clearly terraced.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, connected wings around a shared open space can yield a coherent neighborhood section with public sequence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference has more explicit multi-wing interlock and more void-to-solid richness than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a void and setback upper masses can make a clear ground/public hierarchy.

warnings: The access edge response is semantically weak: the frontage reads more as a side condition than a clearly aligned public threshold.
The void is legible but underscaled, so it risks reading as a slit rather than usable public ground.
Sectional expression is subdued; the mass could better support the program with a clearer carved court or terrace logic.
